title: Year four close: the ways
hook: practice and thought, law and heart, all pointing one direction

segments.voice: Yesterday: humility after learning, and your line: someone knows more. Today, the last day of year four.

A small arrow is stuck to the ceiling of a hotel room, pointing past the wall, past the parking lot, past everything. A traveler unrolls a mat beneath it. Across town, a family lines up mats in a living room by the compass on a phone. In a mosque, the whole building is already turned that way. Different rooms, different reasons for being there. One direction. This year walked many ways into the faith: practice and thought, law and heart. On its last day, here's where they all point.
screen: `AN ARROW ON A HOTEL CEILING.` → `DIFFERENT ROOMS, ONE DIRECTION.` → `WHERE THE WAYS POINT.`

segments.voice: First, the ways this year took. Practice: the pillars, from the inside. Thought: the creed, and the reports with their careful chains. Law: the schools, standing in one row. Heart: its stations and its diseases, and the manners that show it. Then the life cycle, from the call to prayer in a newborn's ear to the last prayer, and a living ummah across the world. Second, the direction. The Qur'an tells the Prophet, in Pickthall's translation: "So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship." That's the qiblah, the Kaaba in Mecca. Every school, every land, every hotel room: one direction in prayer. Third, the direction isn't the whole of it. The same surah says: "It is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West." Then it says, in paraphrase, what righteousness is: believing in Allah and the Last Day, giving wealth out of love to family, orphans, the needy and the traveler, keeping the prayer, keeping promises, and patience in hard times. Creed, charity, prayer, manners and heart, in one verse. Fourth, Who the direction is for. Earlier in the same surah: "Unto Allah belong the East and the West, and whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance." Muslims face the Kaaba because they were told to, and worship Allah, Who is not held by any building. So the ways of this year aren't rival roads. They're many paths through one life, and in prayer they all turn the same way. Tomorrow, year five: the sources themselves.
screen: `PRACTICE, THOUGHT, LAW, HEART.` · `TURN THY FACE: THE QIBLAH.` · `NOT ONLY EAST OR WEST: RIGHTEOUSNESS.` · `WHEREVER YOU TURN, ALLAH'S COUNTENANCE.`

segments.voice: If you know the direction, turn toward it; if not, simply sit where you are, and let one thing from this year come forward that you're grateful to have met: a verse, a person, a habit that stuck. If you pray, you can give thanks for the year in two voluntary rak'ahs, two units of prayer, with the intention of thanks.

Year four close. The pillars, the reports, the schools, the creed, the heart, the manners, the life cycle, the world, and the gathering of it all: one faith, walked many ways, facing one direction. Today's word.
Your line: all roads face the qiblah. Many ways, one direction. Year four is done, and thank you for walking it.

howItsDone: Muslims face the qiblah, toward the Kaaba in Mecca, for every prayer, finding it by the mosque's prayer niche, a compass or an app; some also pray voluntary rak'ahs, or bow in a prostration of thanks, when something good happens.

fork.setup: you're in a hotel room with no arrow and no signal. you want to pray. what do you do?
options: skip the prayer until you find the exact direction.
make your best effort at the direction and pray.
face any wall without a thought.
fork.reveal: jurists teach that an honest effort to find the qiblah is enough, and the Qur'an says: whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance.

original.note: Arabic: the direction faced in prayer, toward the Kaaba in Mecca.

trapdoor: what you thought: the qiblah is just a compass direction.
what it means: one direction for every Muslim's prayer, and a picture of many ways of faith facing the same way.
what a scholar hears: 2:144, turn thy face; 2:177, righteousness is not merely east or west; 2:115, whithersoever ye turn, Allah's Countenance.
recall: a circle that sits to learn

chat.says: Why do Muslims all face one way to pray? Is God inside that building?
options: No. They face the Kaaba because they were told to; wherever you turn, there is Allah's Countenance.
Yes. Muslims hold that God lives inside the Kaaba, so every prayer has to aim at it.
Not really one way. Each school picks its own direction; the Kaaba is just one choice.
chat.meaning: The Qur'an says to turn toward the Kaaba, and also: unto Allah belong the East and the West; whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance.
